title: Part III concept map
h1: Part III Concept Map: Ground It and Let It Act
description: An expandable map of Modules 06–07, connecting RAG retrieval, grounded answers and citations with agent tools, state and human approval.
lead: Part III gives a model access to relevant information and, in controlled cases, application tools. RAG retrieves source material before generation; an agent can coordinate multiple steps. In both cases the application still owns access controls, validation and the decision to execute consequential actions.
story: Prepare, retrieve and present source passages, then check generated claims and citations.
Coordinate tool calls and state within a bounded workflow, with reliability checks and human review.

modules.title: Retrieval-Augmented Generation
modules.tagline: Retrieve relevant sources before generating an answer

topics.title: What is RAG, and why use it?
topics.definition: Retrieval-Augmented Generation supplies selected external information to a model at answer time.
topics.example: Search current help articles for a dispute deadline, then provide relevant passages to the model.
topics.finance: RAG can ground a customer-support draft in current bank policy, but the cited policy still needs verification.
topics.usecase: Question answering over documents that change or are not in the model's training data.
topics.keep: RAG can improve access to evidence; it does not guarantee that retrieval or generation is correct.
connects: the flow has retrieval and generation stages

topics.title: RAG architecture
topics.definition: A RAG pipeline prepares documents, retrieves candidate context, constructs a prompt and generates a response.
topics.example: An ingestion job builds an index; at query time the app embeds the question, searches, filters and sends selected passages.
topics.finance: Separate public help from staff procedures before retrieval, not after a generated answer is produced.
topics.usecase: Designing document-grounded assistants and search-backed applications.
topics.keep: Every stage can fail independently and should be measured and monitored.
connects: selected evidence is passed to the model

topics.title: Document ingestion
topics.definition: Ingestion extracts and normalizes source content and metadata for downstream indexing.
topics.example: Parse Markdown headings, extract a PDF table and attach source ID, audience and revision date.
topics.finance: A revised fee schedule should replace or supersede stale policy text in the searchable corpus.
topics.usecase: Building indexes from policies, manuals, reports and knowledge-base content.
topics.keep: Track provenance, access labels and freshness; extraction errors can become retrieval errors.
connects: ingestion is an offline pipeline stage

topics.title: Text chunking
topics.definition: Chunking splits source documents into units that can be retrieved within model and application limits.
topics.example: Keep a dispute rule and its eligibility exception in the same section-sized chunk.
topics.finance: Separating a fee amount from its waiver condition can lead to an incomplete answer.
topics.usecase: Preparing long content for retrieval and context assembly.
topics.keep: Chunk size, overlap and boundaries should be tested against real questions and source structure.

topics.title: Embedding generation and vector storage
topics.definition: Embedding generation maps chunks to vectors that are stored with identifiers and useful metadata.
topics.example: Store each policy section's vector with a source ID, revision and audience label.
topics.finance: A bank can re-index amended policies while preserving version information for auditing.
topics.usecase: Making document passages searchable by semantic similarity.
topics.keep: Keep the embedding model and index version aligned, and retain source provenance.
connects: the chunk is the indexed unit

topics.title: Retrieval
topics.definition: Retrieval selects and ranks candidate source passages for a query, often using filters and a top-k limit.
topics.example: Retrieve the three most relevant current public help sections for a customer's question.
topics.finance: Apply the customer's authorized audience before searching staff-only content.
topics.usecase: RAG context selection, search results and evidence gathering.
topics.keep: Relevant-looking passages can still be stale, incomplete or incorrect; evaluate retrieval separately.

topics.title: Prompt construction
topics.definition: Prompt construction combines instructions, user input and retrieved context into a model request.
topics.example: Label each source, ask for a concise answer and tell the model to say when supplied sources do not answer.
topics.finance: Use clear boundaries between a customer's message and retrieved policy text.
topics.usecase: Grounded question answering and controlled summarization.
topics.keep: Retrieved content is untrusted input; prompt wording alone is not a security boundary.
connects: the model receives the constructed request
both systems use instructions and context

topics.title: Response generation
topics.definition: Generation produces an answer from the model's instructions, input and any retrieved context.
topics.example: Ask for an answer supported by supplied policy passages and a clear abstention when evidence is missing.
topics.finance: A response about a dispute deadline should reflect the current source, not a plausible model guess.
topics.usecase: Natural-language answers, summaries and drafts over retrieved information.
topics.keep: A grounded prompt can still produce unsupported claims; inspect and evaluate the output.
connects: instructions and context shape the request

topics.title: Citation and source attribution
topics.definition: Citation and attribution connect a response to source identifiers so users can inspect supporting material.
topics.example: Render a link to the policy section used to answer a question about card disputes.
topics.finance: A support agent can compare a drafted policy explanation with the bank's approved source.
topics.usecase: Auditable knowledge answers and evidence review.
topics.keep: A citation can point to a real source without proving the source entails the claim.
connects: attribution is part of grounded answering

modules.title: Building AI Agents
modules.tagline: Coordinate model decisions and application tools within explicit boundaries

topics.title: What is an AI agent? Agent vs chatbot
topics.definition: An agent uses a model to select steps or tools toward a task, while application code runs tools and enforces constraints.
topics.example: An assistant can look up a customer's card status and request a freeze through a separate approval step.
topics.finance: A bank agent should not be allowed to move money merely because a model generated a tool call.
topics.usecase: Multi-step workflows where tool access adds value beyond a single response.
topics.keep: More autonomy adds complexity and risk; use the least autonomy that solves the task.

topics.title: Reasoning and planning
topics.definition: Planning decomposes a task into steps or tool requests; the application should bound and validate that process.
topics.example: List allowed cards, inspect one card's status and ask for approval before freezing it.
topics.finance: A support workflow can require verified identity and policy checks before a card action.
topics.usecase: Tasks that need ordered information gathering or controlled tool execution.
topics.keep: A generated plan is not proof of correct reasoning or permission to act.

topics.title: Tool calling for agents
topics.definition: Tool calling lets a model request a named function with arguments that application code can inspect.
topics.example: The model requests card_status with a last-four identifier from the app's own card list.
topics.finance: The server must check that the card belongs to the authenticated customer before returning status.
topics.usecase: Connecting assistants to databases, APIs and approved actions.
topics.keep: Validate tool names and arguments, enforce authorization and limit side effects.
connects: tool selection can follow a plan

topics.title: Agent workflows
topics.definition: An agent workflow defines how model calls, tools, state and control flow interact.
topics.example: A bounded loop receives a tool request, validates it, executes it and returns the result to the model.
topics.finance: A card-freeze workflow can separate lookup, approval and the actual state change.
topics.keep: Explicit state transitions and stop conditions are safer than an unbounded loop.

topics.title: State and memory
topics.definition: State is information retained for a task or session; memory may be passed back into later model requests.
topics.example: Store a conversation identifier and recent turns, with a defined expiration and deletion policy.
topics.finance: Customer conversation history needs access controls, retention limits and secure storage.
topics.usecase: Multi-turn assistants and workflows that span requests.
topics.keep: A model does not automatically remember prior calls; application-managed memory has privacy and cost trade-offs.
connects: later actions depend on earlier results
retrieval adds external context rather than session memory

topics.title: Multi-step tasks
topics.definition: A multi-step task performs several dependent operations before returning a result.
topics.example: Check a card, ask for consent, execute a freeze and confirm the resulting status.
topics.finance: A dispute case may require identity, transaction and policy checks before a human review.
topics.usecase: Workflows with dependencies, conditional branches or multiple tools.
topics.keep: Each step needs a bounded retry policy, clear failure behavior and outcome verification.

topics.title: Human-in-the-loop workflows
topics.definition: Human review inserts a person into a workflow to approve, reject or correct a decision or action.
topics.example: Show a freeze preview derived from application data, then ask the customer to approve before executing it.
topics.finance: A consequential account action should have a defined consent and escalation path.
topics.usecase: High-impact decisions, ambiguous cases and actions with external side effects.
topics.keep: Approval must be bound to the exact action and trusted data; a prompt asking for consent is not enough by itself.

topics.title: Agent reliability
topics.definition: Agent reliability uses bounded behavior, validation, explicit errors and measured outcomes to reduce failures.
topics.example: Limit tool-loop steps, reject unknown functions and report a failed tool call rather than claiming success.
topics.finance: Compare the final customer-facing response with the actual recorded account action.
topics.usecase: Production workflows that must handle model and dependency failures.
topics.keep: A fluent final answer is not evidence that the requested operation succeeded.
connects: source checks are another reliability measure
